passage:
Pilar: Friendly reminder that quiet hours start at 10. Someone's been running a washer at midnight.
Dev: Agreed, that's really inconsiderate. Heads-up though, I'm having people over Saturday and it'll probably go until 1. It's my birthday, so that's different.
Ruth: Noted, I guess.
cue: It's my birthday, so that's different.
explanation: Dev agrees quiet hours matter, then exempts himself because it's his birthday. A neighbor trying to sleep is kept awake just the same, whatever the occasion.

whyNot.fal_moving_the_goalposts: Dev isn't raising a bar someone already cleared; he keeps the rule for others and waives it for himself.

passage: Real talk for my coaching clients: if you want results, you log every single bite, weekends included. No excuses, no "I'll remember it later." (I don't track on weekends myself, but weekends are family time for me, so that's a different situation.) Consistency is everything!
cue: weekends are family time for me, so that's a different situation
explanation: Marisa demands that clients log every bite, then excuses herself because weekends are family time. Her clients have family weekends too, and that doesn't change what anyone eats.

whyNot.fal_no_true_scotsman: Marisa isn't redefining who counts as a real client; she holds others to a rule and gives herself a pass.

title: Office days starting next month
passage: Hi team, thanks for your patience while we reviewed the hybrid pilot. The survey showed handoffs slowed when people were rarely in the same room, so starting next month everyone will be in the office Monday through Thursday. I'll keep working from home on Tuesdays, since a lot of my work is focused planning. Thanks, Celeste
cue: I'll keep working from home on Tuesdays, since a lot of my work is focused planning
explanation: Celeste's rule rests on handoffs between people, and she's part of those handoffs. "Focused planning" isn't a relevant difference; much of her team does focused work too.

whyNot.fal_no_true_scotsman: Celeste isn't redefining who counts as part of the team; she applies a rule to everyone but herself without a relevant reason.

source: Mayor Constance Ilori · Dunmarrow drought briefing
passage: The reservoir is at 31%, its lowest level in fifteen years, so starting Monday, residential lawn watering is limited to one day a week. I know that's hard. The one exception will be the Copperbeck golf course, which keeps its daily schedule. That course has been the pride of this town for fifty years, and I won't see it go brown.
cue: That course has been the pride of this town for fifty years
explanation: The limit exists because water is scarce, and a golf course uses far more than a lawn. Constance exempts it out of civic pride, which has nothing to do with how much water is left.

whyNot.fal_moving_the_goalposts: No one met a standard that then got raised; Constance sets one rule for residents and waives it for a favored course.

source: Lars Whitfield, senior engineer · Tuesday standup
passage: Quick reminder, everyone: two approvals on every code change, no exceptions, because that's how we catch the bugs we can't see in our own code. For tonight's urgent billing fix I'm going to release it on my own review, though. I wrote that code, so I know it better than anyone who'd be reviewing it.
cue: I wrote that code, so I know it better than anyone who'd be reviewing it
explanation: Lars says reviews exist because authors miss bugs in their own code, and writing the code makes him exactly that author. His expertise sounds relevant, but the rule's purpose still applies to him.

whyNot.fal_moving_the_goalposts: Lars isn't changing the standard after someone met it; he keeps the review rule for everyone else and waives it for himself.

title: Still my favorite, even on an off night
passage: Regular readers know my rule: I review the meal I got, not the meal a place is capable of, and excuses don't count. Tonight at Trattoria Belvane the pasta came out cold and the service was slow, but they were down two cooks, and I've been coming here for nine years. I'm going on what I know this kitchen can do. Five stars.
cue: I'm going on what I know this kitchen can do
explanation: Desmond's own rule is to rate the meal served and ignore excuses. For his longtime favorite, he accepts the staffing excuse and rates what the kitchen can do instead.

whyNot.fal_no_true_scotsman: Desmond doesn't redefine what counts as a real restaurant; he suspends his own reviewing rule for a place he loves.

title: Late fees this month
passage: Hi everyone, our lease charges a $50 fee for rent paid after the 5th. This month I'm waiving it for every tenant who paid late, because the payment portal was down from the 3rd to the 6th, so nobody could pay on time, which is what the fee exists to encourage. The fee applies as usual next month. Odalys
cue: the payment portal was down from the 3rd to the 6th, so nobody could pay on time
explanation: Odalys makes an exception for a reason tied to the fee's purpose: the outage made paying on time impossible. It applies to every affected tenant, and the rule returns next month.

whyNot.fal_special_pleading: The exception rests on a relevant, stated difference and covers everyone affected, not just a favored person.

passage:
Mom: Phones in the basket, everyone, dinner's ready.
Ayesha: Mine stays on the table tonight. I'm the on-call vet this weekend, and if the clinic calls, an animal could be in trouble.
Jun: You're always the strictest about the basket!
Ayesha: And I still am. Anyone who's on call gets the same pass.
cue: I'm the on-call vet this weekend
explanation: Ayesha exempts herself, but for a reason that matters (she may be needed for an emergency) and she offers the same exception to anyone in her position.

whyNot.fal_special_pleading: Ayesha's exception rests on a relevant difference and applies to anyone on call, so it isn't a double standard.
